title: T2 Spike: pi-durable afterResponse document write, pi.usage reads, child conversation enumeration
description: Plan: docs/COST_ACCOUNTING.md sections 3.2 and 4 (S0). Verify with throwaway code outside conversation/src: (1) can GenerationHooks.afterResponse (node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-durable/dist/harness/types.d.ts) write a defineDoc in the commit that records the response; (2) harness.usage() and the pi.usage document contents for aborted, errored and compaction calls; (3) enumerate task-owned child conversations and forks through IndexedStorage (conversation/src/storage/indexed-storage.ts l2 CT# and l3 CC# indexes); (4) decide channel-total design (GSI vs sibling item). comments.author: home
comments.text: Spike done, PR 536 (not merged). Findings: (1) afterResponse runs before the response commit with a read-only HookApi; a record it writes is a separate commit (undocumented runtime commit), not atomic. The assistant entry and pi.usage are the atomic part. (2) Keyed derivation from entries (key entry-<id>) is idempotent across retry and a takeover with a new fence; stale owner is rejected with OwnershipLost. (3) Keyed family documents are readable by key via a reader session with no replay; use fork initial; child conversations enumerate by ownerTaskId, ownerConversationId and whole partition; harness.usage sums children. (4) usage plus pi-ai cost are enough for our own price book; compaction spend is only in pi.usage (no entry, no hook). Recommendation: no hook, derive at conclude/fail/yield/park/takeover. Details in docs/COST_SPIKE_PI_DURABLE.md. Leaving in_progress until the PR merges.

The ledger row matches the session records, the earlier computer-owner double count is gone, and the owner role policy for the cost partition is deployed.
